source: If this explanation is causal, it is informative. This explanation is informative. Therefore this explanation is causal.

reconstruction.title: Affirming the Consequent in Explanation Causality

claims.text: If this explanation is causal, it is informative.

evidence.quote: If this explanation is causal, it is informative.

claims.interpretation_note: Conditional statement establishing a sufficient condition for informativeness.
Assertion of the consequent in the conditional statement.
Conclusion derived from the premises, committing the fallacy of affirming the consequent.

translations.reason: Translating the conditional 'If this explanation is causal, it is informative' as material implication between atomic propositions
Direct translation of the assertion 'This explanation is informative' as an atomic proposition
Direct translation of the conclusion 'This explanation is causal' as an atomic proposition

interpretation_notes: Treated 'causal' and 'informative' as atomic propositions since no internal logical structure is present in the source claims
The argument structure corresponds to the formal fallacy of affirming the consequent (from (P→Q) and Q, concluding P)
